sections.overview: The ornate wobbegong is a benthic carpet shark of eastern Australia and Papua New Guinea.
sections.identification: Its flattened, patterned body bears branched skin lobes beside the head; it is generally smaller than the similar Gulf wobbegong, O. halei.
sections.habitat: It occupies bays, reefs and offshore islands in inshore and continental-shelf waters, often sheltering among complex rocky structures.
sections.diet: A New South Wales study found a diet mainly of bony fishes, with cephalopods and other cartilaginous fishes also present.
sections.behavior: It shows strong attachment to particular reef sites, a trait that also makes it susceptible to fishing pressure.
sections.reproduction: It is viviparous and has low reproductive output; Australian assessments report litters of roughly 4–18 pups and a multi-year cycle.
sections.ecology: The Gulf wobbegong was once grouped with this species but is now separate; see O. halei for the reciprocal comparison and distinguishing traits.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN category is Least Concern, although New South Wales lists the species as Vulnerable after historical fishing declines.
